A1.justification: Despite retitling and extensive reorganization, both PDFs describe the same COCA research. Their main texts, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching.

before.justification: v1 reports original safety and helpfulness experiments in Tables 1–3, component ablations, representation visualizations, and additional empirical results in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original COCA experiments and adds linear-probe measurements, controlled comparisons, data-volume ablations, white-box attack results, and additional model evaluations.

M1.justification: The core structured concept-reasoning pipeline and supervised objective remain unchanged. v2 adds an implemented COCA+STAIR variant that feeds STAIR's Problem Analysis into the COCA reasoning stage, and a safety-first prefix for the reasoning-model variant. These are limited procedural extensions; the expanded adapter-training description primarily clarifies implementation.

E1.justification: v2 adds gradient-based white-box GCG attacks as a distinct adversarial scenario (Appendix E, Table 9). The training datasets and existing safety, WildJailbreak, math, coding, and XsTesT coverage are retained. Additional model sizes and reasoning backbones change model configurations rather than dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds STAIR to the main LoFiT comparison in Table 1, Prompt-Only and COCA-SFT-only controls in Tables 4–5, and SAFEPATH-style LoFiT and STAR-1 comparisons for the reasoning model in Table 10. These substantially expand the evaluated comparator set beyond v1's retained intervention and SRG baselines.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs include probes trained on illegal/benign prompts and tested on jailbreak/benign prompts, reporting maximum ROC–AUC across layers; controls separating COCA supervision from active intervention; 1K/5K/10K safety-training budgets; and 3B, 14B, and reasoning-model configurations. The original training and decoding settings are largely retained, so these additions do not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds quantitative separability and covariance diagnostics (Tables 3 and 12), tag-removal and STAIR-composition ablations (Figure 3b), supervision-versus-intervention controls (Table 4), data-volume sensitivity (Table 8), and GCG robustness testing (Table 9). Appendix F also adds perplexity evidence for RR's incoherent outputs. The original PCA, fixed-reasoning, and over-refusal analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The added experiments do not introduce a new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial results, including Prompt-Only and COCA-SFT-only OOD ASRs of 30.9% and 16.2% against the retained full-model result of 10.4% (Table 4), plus probe, GCG, scaling, and reasoning-model results. Existing results also change: v1 Table 3 to v2 Table 5 revises COCA's Cipher ASR from 2.5% to 1.5% and LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct's average from 17.7% to 14.8%. These are reporting revisions, not established performance gains from rerunning the method.

T1.justification: v1's assertion that every nonconstant independent eraser has greater distortion than the constant mean is replaced by a conditional-mean projection lower bound and a conditional strictness statement in v2 Theorem 2.2. The linear-erasure statement is narrowed from statistical independence to linear guardedness. Appendix H.2 replaces the Taylor-based derivation with a Gaussian/Stein-identity argument and adds an approximate-isotropy error bound.

C1.justification: The abstracts, introductions, and conclusions retain the central claims: nonlinear entanglement limits faithful intervention, structured COCA reasoning concentrates harmful concepts, and COCA improves jailbreak robustness while preserving benign capabilities. The formal theory changes substantially, but the headline contributions remain essentially the same.

C2.justification: v2 newly attributes residual Code Attack vulnerability to obfuscated concept identification, interprets supervision and intervention as complementary, and argues that longer reasoning alone is insufficient. It adds limitations concerning forged benign concept tags, untested 70B-plus models, teacher quality, and safety-taxonomy variation. Section 2.3 also expands the connection between the theoretical two-head abstraction and autoregressive training.

D1.justification: v2 clarifies frozen-base, trainable-adapter training and active intervention at inference, adds an explicit public-code statement and repository address, and reports annotation costs of roughly 30 A100 GPU-hours or $40 for 70K examples. Conversely, it omits v1's stated 400-example ID total and explicit pattern-matching definition of over-refusal. These are disclosure changes rather than demonstrated changes to retained experiments.

R1.justification: v2 adds targeted positioning against concept alignment, contrastive representation learning, and Intent-FT, alongside references for SAFEPATH, STAR-1, and expanded limitations. The central positioning of COCA as data-level restructuring that enables representation intervention remains. SRG's updated title and venue represent the same previously cited work.

P1.justification: The title changes, and the introduction and method narrative are extensively rewritten around concept-centric alignment and representation geometry. Related work moves after the method, the theoretical appendices are consolidated, and guidelines are reordered. New implementation explanations, limitations, impact discussion, and manuscript-preparation disclosure substantially alter the document's organization and exposition.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a two-column main layout, redraws Figure 1 with an explicit geometry illustration, and reorganizes Table 1 into side-by-side model groups with change columns. It combines the original ablation and over-refusal charts with a new component panel in Figure 3 and adds several tables. Figure 2 becomes an explicitly labeled two-panel comparison, while the original three-panel visualizations remain in the appendix.

improvement.justification: The new linear probes and Prompt-Only/SFT-only/full-model controls in Tables 3–4 substantially strengthen evidence that v1 supported mainly through visualizations and combined supervision/intervention comparisons. GCG and data-volume tests add useful validation, while revised derivations expose assumptions more clearly. Some measurement details are lost, and broad impossibility wording still exceeds the revised theorem's conditional scope, but the gains in experimental support and transparency constitute a substantial overall improvement.
